acceptance_summary: Global activation: toggle must be reliable; PTT (hold) only where capability-proven via P0F, with truthful capability exposure.
Capture microphone audio without blocking the UI/input event loop.
Stream tentative transcription where the selected engine supports it.

Deliver final text with capability-based backend selection (semantic/clipboard/virtual-keyboard/etc) and bounded fallback; Unicode/multiline per backend capability, Inbox final sink, no silent broad input privilege default.
Preserve raw, corrected, and delivered transcript variants per committed session.
Optional in-memory audio pre-roll to prevent clipped first syllables.
Audio policy for Linux 1.0: leave must work plus at least one proven crash-safe duck or pause; additional policies (mute/smart/etc) deferred post-1.0 unless qualified.
Recover unsent dictation after process failure where feasible.
Dictation Inbox fallback when no writable target is available.
User can cancel an active session without stale output.
Microphones support deterministic ranking, explicit user override, hotplug detection, and bounded fallback/recovery.
Playback streams that appear while duck/pause/mute policy is active inherit the current session policy without polling races.
Final text delivery applies deterministic target-aware cursor spacing/punctuation without destructive blind whitespace changes.
Modes are declarative pipelines, not UI-only presets.
Built-in Raw and Clean modes in 1.0.
Message, Professional, Email, Developer, Prompt, Compose, Notes, Translate and Custom modes in 1.x.
App Profiles select a default mode/policy based on active application/context.
Selected-text transformations support replace + reliable undo.
Smart self-correction/backtracking: phrases such as “actually”, “scratch that”, “make that” can repair recent speech.
Confidence-directed correction can repair low-confidence spans without reprocessing the entire transcript.
Deterministic text processing is preferred over LLM calls for simple formatting/rules.
Context-aware decoding/biasing is used when an ASR backend supports it.
Language/script/translation/locale settings are separate, capability-driven and reject unsupported combinations honestly.
Advanced scoped dictionary (global/language/app/mode/project/team) — deferred post-1.0; basic dictionary remains in FUN-041 scope.
Spoken aliases/pronunciations map to canonical forms.
Correction Memory can propose learning repeated user corrections.
Learning weights decay with staleness and scope.
Snippets support static text and typed variables.
Shareable Mode/Profile/Pack format is versioned.
Smart templates with typed fields and field navigation are a post-1.0 workflow capability.
Domain packs can bundle vocabulary, pronunciations, Modes, snippets/templates, and deterministic rules in a validated versioned format after 1.0.
Structured dictation into schema-aware forms/JSON/tables is a post-1.0 capability.
Patch-based streaming insertion may apply stable transcript deltas instead of replacing the entire tentative region after 1.0.
Context Fabric supports providers for app, window, selection, surrounding text, clipboard, project/repository, personal vocabulary and future integrations.
Every context provider declares sensitivity and permission requirements.
Modes request only required context fields.
Project Context may index filenames, symbols, dependencies and repository terminology with user control.
Context must never be sent remotely unless policy explicitly permits it.
Command Mode supports a typed safe action API.
Hybrid Mode combines dictation and explicit command grammar.
Spell Mode supports literal character/phonetic entry.
Dynamic “What can I say?” exposes context-specific commands.
Voice Workflows are permissioned, typed multi-step actions.
Anchored Dictation can keep a target while user views another app where platform APIs permit.
Number/grid UI overlays are a later accessibility capability, not a 1.0 requirement.
Long-running meeting/session capture.
Microphone + optional system audio capture with explicit permissions.
Speaker diarization; optional speaker recognition later.
Export TXT/Markdown/JSON/SRT/VTT.
Optional local summary, decisions, tasks, questions and commitments.
Live captions and subtitle-file workflows reuse the same media pipeline.
An optional phone-as-microphone companion may pair over the local network using authenticated encrypted transport with explicit revoke/reset semantics after 1.0.
A public extension SDK is post-1.0 and must derive from stable internal contracts with explicit sandbox/permission/versioning policy.
Optional remote/local-network compute nodes are post-1.0 and require authenticated encrypted transport plus the same per-request privacy/policy checks as local provider selection.
Optional team/shared knowledge packs and policy hierarchy are post-1.0 and must not complicate or disable single-user offline Narrivy.
First successful dictation must be achievable without exposing runtime/backend jargon.
Linux 1.0 navigation is Home, Dictation, Models, Applications, History, Settings, Diagnostics; deferred Snippets/Integrations are not working top-level placeholders.
Advanced technical controls use progressive disclosure.
Overlay never steals focus in normal dictation.
Overlay reflects listening/processing/error only when useful; avoid flashing transient stages.
Local/cloud processing state is visible.
User-facing errors provide recovery action, not just technical detail.
Search/command-palette access to settings/actions.
Destructive AI transformations have one-step undo.
Capability tests can be launched individually from Diagnostics.
Measure hotkey→listening, speech→partial, release→raw, release→committed separately.
Target hotkey acknowledgement <30 ms on supported reference hardware.
Target capture-ready <50 ms for a warm running service.
Target visible listening feedback <100 ms.
Target first partial <250 ms when engine/platform supports streaming.
Keep audio capture real-time thread free of blocking I/O and model inference.
Model residency states: Hot, Warm, Cold.
Compiled/optimized cache has robust invalidation/ownership and safely cleans unreferenced benchmark losing variants while preserving source, selected/shared/pinned and CPU fallback assets.
Avoid unnecessary device transfers and duplicate audio conversion.
Pipeline can prepare context/model/output concurrently.
Session state machine is explicit and testable.
Failure of overlay must not terminate audio/ASR service.
Failure of one text-delivery backend triggers bounded fallback.
Suspend/resume and device hotplug are supported lifecycle events.
Audio duck/pause state is restored after clean exit and abnormal failure wherever technically possible.
Active session journal allows recovery of unsent results.
Every background worker has cancellation and shutdown semantics.
Support report excludes transcript/audio/context content by default.
Temporary audio duck/pause/mute mutations have crash-safe restoration metadata/watchdog behavior and are repaired after abrupt termination wherever the platform makes reliable restoration possible.
Portable core crates compile on Linux, Windows and macOS CI targets from Phase 0.
OS-specific APIs exist only in platform adapters.
Desktop/frontend is a client of application APIs, not the owner of core domain behavior.
IPC transport is hidden from domain logic behind a portable abstraction; Linux uses same-user Unix domain sockets.
Capabilities drive UI instead of OS-name branching.
Compute/runtime backends are replaceable capability modules across CPU and qualified NPU/dGPU/iGPU paths without core coupling or public Rust dylib ABI.

Post-1.0 native Windows and macOS proof clients must reuse the portable domain/protocol contracts rather than fork/rewrite product logic, including a Windows named-pipe IPC transport behind the same abstraction and compile proof of the portable crates on Windows/macOS (PORT-001).
Local processing is default.
History retention is user-configurable and can be disabled globally or by Privacy Zone.
Privacy Zones override Mode/Profile/plugin cloud permissions.
Cloud-bound data is declared before use and visible in UI.
Secrets are never stored in regular config files.
Logs/diagnostics redact content by default.
Plugin permissions are explicit and enforced.
Model/plugin manifests support checksum/signature verification.
Network access from sandboxed extensions is deny-by-default.
Supply-chain and dependency-license checks are release gates.
Local IPC accepts only the intended local user/session and applies least-privilege endpoint permissions plus peer validation where the OS supports it.
Imported model/plugin/pack archives are treated as untrusted and reject path traversal, unsafe links, and integrity mismatches before extraction/use.
Full keyboard operation.
Screen-reader labels and semantic roles.
Reduced motion.
Scalable text/UI and high-DPI correctness.
High-contrast compatible palette and focus visibility.
Critical state is not conveyed only by color or animation.
Hands-free roadmap must not compromise normal privacy/reliability defaults.
Every release-gated requirement maps to a named automated or manual verification and evidence location.
Architecture-boundary tests inspect source and dependency metadata so forbidden framework/OS/runtime coupling cannot silently enter portable crates.
Core session, policy, pipeline, IPC protocol, and fallback contracts have deterministic unit/contract tests independent of real hardware.
Linux integration tests exercise global-trigger, capture lifecycle, audio restoration, text-delivery routing, and target-application compatibility on reference sessions.
ASR/model/device qualification records correctness, streaming/final behavior, timestamps where supported, warm/cold behavior, failure/fallback, and quality/performance baselines.
Failure-injection tests cover daemon/client loss, text-delivery failure, device loss, corrupt cache/model metadata, and interrupted sessions without losing recoverable text.
Accessibility and UI acceptance include keyboard-only, focus, semantics, scaling, contrast, reduced-motion, error/recovery, and representative assistive-technology checks.
Phase and release gates fail closed: missing tests/evidence/status cannot be interpreted as a pass.
The Integrated Dictation Beta gate requires a real Linux vertical slice: global trigger → microphone → real local ASR → processing → external-target delivery or Inbox fallback.
Linux 1.0 qualification requires release-artifact E2E evidence on the Pop!_OS COSMIC/Wayland reference environment plus CPU fallback; GNOME/Wayland and other distributions follow post-release.
A non-destructive doctor reports host/toolchain/desktop/audio/portal/compute capabilities and actionable remediation without exposing user content.
Linux 1.0 ships a tested .deb as its single installation artifact (owner decision 2026-08-22: no AppImage/portable package); AppImage/RPM/AUR/Nix are follow-on unless promoted by ADR.
Install, launch, upgrade, rollback/recovery, and uninstall preserve or remove user data according to documented policy and never silently destroy history/configuration.
Release artifacts have checksums, dependency/license inventory, SBOM, immutable build identity, and signing/provenance where release infrastructure permits.
Release notes list verified supported environments/capabilities and known limitations; untested compatibility is never presented as supported.
Application and configuration/model schema migrations are versioned, testable, backward-safe where promised, and recoverable from interrupted migration.
Saved Pipelines are first-class versioned typed graphs; multiple coexist with explicit bounded module fallbacks.
Trigger bindings address pipeline IDs and support independent toggle/hold semantics where platform capability proves them.
Deterministic correction is separate from optional local/remote LLM processing; raw text is recoverable and generative output guarded.
Lean default pipeline works without backend jargon while Advanced supports compatible module substitution and user compute choices.
Optional encrypted account sync preserves account-free local operation and syncs portable intent rather than binaries/host caches.
Shadow pipeline can evaluate an alternate graph without delivering output and recommend changes from measured evidence.
Versioned full/partial settings and pipeline import/export excludes secrets/host caches by default and previews missing downloads.
Module/runtime/model/pipeline artifacts are distinct versioned dependency-resolved resources independent of download location.
Remote transcript and context permissions are independent opt-ins per pipeline/profile/privacy zone; text provider does not receive audio implicitly.
Downloads use trusted immutable registry metadata and expected integrity/signature data; mutable arbitrary URLs do not gain executable trust.
